purpose: The closed community vocabulary, and the rules by which every person and household in data/residents/ is given a community from evidence THIS LAYER ALREADY HOLDS.
what_this_is_not: NOT a reading of any new source, and not a reconstruction of anybody. Nothing here mints a person, upgrades a confidence or invents a citation. Every value is read off a field already committed — a household's `origin` block, or a reconstructed person's own `reconstruction.community` — and is graded no higher than the field it was read from. Where the layer says nothing, the value is `unknown` and stays `unknown`. The cohort tickets T-1376 (Native and Metis), T-1377 (free Black) and T-1378 (businesses, Irish and German shares) are where new readings happen.

the_tier_ladder.reconstruction_community: A reconstructed person drawn from a name pool carries the pool's community on the record already. Tier `reconstructed`, because the person is.
the_tier_ladder.stated_community: The origin sentence STATES a community or a descent. Tier is the origin block's own confidence, uncapped — the sentence is the evidence.
the_tier_ladder.origin_region: The origin sentence states a PLACE. A place is not a community, so the reading is an inference about the person: tier is the origin block's confidence CAPPED AT `inferred`. An attested origin therefore yields an inferred community.
the_tier_ladder.none: No rule fires. Value `unknown`, tier null, and the basis says which of the two reasons it was — no origin recorded, or an origin this file cannot read.

who_a_household_origin_speaks_for.note: A household's origin is where its FAMILY came from. It is not evidence about the boarder, lodger, servant, clerk, apprentice or journeyman under its roof, nor about an unnamed `household_member`, and this pass does not extend it to them — they read `unknown` unless their own record carries a community. A STATED descent (Caldwell's, Robinson's) narrows further still, to the head and the relations who descend from the same parents: a wife does not take her husband's descent.

vocabulary.label: Native (nation not stated)
vocabulary.note: THE SOURCE SAYS INDIAN AND SAYS NOTHING FURTHER. The Illinois State Archives roll of Black Hawk War enrollments at Chicago heads a company of ninety-four men INDIAN and distinguishes no nation among them; T-1376 cards those men and writes this term rather than choosing one of the three below for them. A card that later reaches a nation replaces it. Every person carrying it is review_required and touches_removal.

vocabulary.label: Potawatomi
vocabulary.note: A nation, written only where a source states it. T-1376 read the one roll this corpus holds that names Native people at Chicago in numbers and it states no nation, so no card carries this term yet; `native` above is what that roll supports.

vocabulary.label: Ottawa (Odawa)
vocabulary.note: A nation, written only where a source states it. No card carries it: see `native` above for what the 1832 roll supports.

vocabulary.label: Ojibwe
vocabulary.note: A nation, written only where a source states it. No card carries it: see `native` above for what the 1832 roll supports.

vocabulary.label: Metis
vocabulary.note: A person of mixed Native and European descent in the Great Lakes trade, which is how the two cards that carry it are worded by their own sources.

vocabulary.label: French Canadian
vocabulary.note: The Great Lakes French trade community of the Detroit, Mackinac and Milwaukee country. NOT `born in France` — see the Lyons rule.

vocabulary.label: Free Black
vocabulary.note: T-1377 wrote it. Caton's 1833 defence of 'six or seven free coloured men' is the FLOOR of the bracket and the 1840 census's 53 free coloured persons the ceiling; the `free_black` sub-stage of stage `underdocumented` writes the floor — 7 households, 13 people, 2 firms, every one reconstructed and review_required. Nobody carrying this value is a person a source names, and the head-room to the ceiling is deliberately left open. docs/RESEARCH/black_chicago_1835.md.

vocabulary.label: New England
vocabulary.note: New England proper. The reconstruction's name pool of the same id covers New England AND New York together, so a pool-drawn person reads `yankee` at a coarser grain than a card whose origin names a state.

vocabulary.label: New York State
vocabulary.note: New York State, the Erie Canal corridor the town's origin distribution is built on.

vocabulary.label: German
vocabulary.note: No card carries it yet — the register's German Catholic rows are T-1378's to check against the model.

vocabulary.label: Southern
vocabulary.note: Virginia, Maryland, the Carolinas, Kentucky and the District — the slave states and the District, taken together as the period did.

vocabulary.label: Other
vocabulary.note: A community the layer's evidence names and this vocabulary has no term for. Every use is listed in the rules below; none is a shrug.

vocabulary.label: Unknown
vocabulary.note: The layer holds no evidence of this person's community. The honest majority value, and the one the cohort tickets exist to shrink.

pool_aliases._note: data/reconstruction/1835_invented_name_pools.json names its third pool `french_colonial` and 121 reconstructed persons carry that string. The pool is this vocabulary's `french_canadian`; the records are not rewritten for a rename, they are resolved here.

stated_community.origin: Detroit; his father an Irish officer in the British army, his mother Potawatomi
stated_community.note: Billy Caldwell (Sauganash). The sentence states the parentage — an Irish father in the British service and a Potawatomi mother — and `metis` is this vocabulary's term for a person of that descent in the Great Lakes trade. It does not replace `potawatomi`: Caldwell's standing among the Potawatomi is a separate claim that T-1376 reads and records.

stated_community.origin: Mackinaw; his father a Scots trader, his mother an Ottawa woman
stated_community.note: Alexander Robinson (Che-che-pin-qua). Same reading as Caldwell's: the sentence states a Scots father and an Ottawa mother. His Potawatomi and Ottawa standing is T-1376's to record.

stated_community.origin: Detroit and the Milwaukee trade, of a French colonial family
stated_community.note: Col. Jean Baptiste Beaubien. `of a French colonial family` is a statement about the household's community and not only about where it came from.

stated_community.origin: A French-descended trading family of the Detroit and Milwaukee country
stated_community.note: Same sentence in another card's wording.

stated_community.origin: The French colonial settlements of the Detroit and Milwaukee country
stated_community.note: The reconstruction spec's own band for the Great Lakes French trade population, written into three reconstructed households' origin.

origin_region.origin: New England, by way of the garrison church at Fort Brady, Sault Ste Marie
Windsor, Vermont, by way of Montreal
Sackett's Harbor, New York; born at Guilford, Vermont
County Kerry, Ireland, by way of Lancashire, Dublin, Quebec, Montreal, New York, Virginia and Newark
Lyons, France, by way of St Louis and St Mary's of the Barrens, Missouri
origin_region.note: FRENCH-BORN IS NOT FRENCH-CANADIAN. `french_canadian` in this vocabulary is the Great Lakes trade community of the Detroit, Mackinac and Milwaukee country; a man out of Lyons by way of the Missouri seminary belongs to neither that community nor any other term here.
Pennsylvania, for the same reason as the Mid-Atlantic band above.

New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania stock that is neither New England nor Southern. THE VOCABULARY HAS NO MID-ATLANTIC TERM and this rule will not force 112 households into `new_york`, which is a different claim from the one the origin makes. Recorded as `other` until the owner rules on the term.
Ohio, Indiana and the Illinois country — the western American stock the reconstruction spec names as its own band, and again a band this vocabulary has no term for. Not `southern`, not `yankee`.

unreadable_origin.note: Madore Benjamin Beaubien. Born at Chicago to Jean Baptiste Beaubien — whose own origin states a French colonial family — and, the literature says, a Potawatomi mother. THE LAYER DOES NOT SAY THAT HERE, so this pass reads `unknown` rather than inherit a community down a parentage the record has not written. T-1376 is the ticket that reads the sources and cards this household properly; when it does, this row should stop being unknown.

unreadable_origin.origin: Chicago, by way of Fort Winnebago
unreadable_origin.note: Born or last resident at the settlement itself. Says nothing about community.

Detroit alone says a place and not a community: the town held a French colonial population, an American garrison and territorial officers, and Yankee and New York merchants passing through. The origin does not separate them and this pass will not guess.

coverage_rule: Every distinct `origin.value` in data/residents/ must appear exactly once across `stated_community`, `origin_region` and `unreadable_origin`. tools/derive_person_community.py --check fails when one does not, so a new origin string cannot enter the layer without somebody deciding what it means.
